newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila privatisation earnings fall short of target.
newsitem.headline: Manila privatisation earnings fall short of target.

text.p: Revenues from the privatisation programme fell 45 percent below target during the first eight months of this year, the Philippines' Bureau of Treasury said on Sunday.
Proceeds reached 4.232 billion pesos or 3.478 billion pesos short of the 7.710- billion peso target for the same period, the bureau said in a statement.

Delays in the sale of several big-ticket items including the Philippine Phosphate Fertiliser Inc (Philphos) and the Philippine Associated Smelting and Refining Corp (PASAR) accounted for the shortfall, it said.
Philphos is 50-percent owned by the National Development Co, an equity investment arm of the government, and 50 percent by the Nauru government.
PASAR is 41 percent owned by another government-controlled firm with 32 percent owned by a Japanese consortium made up of Itochu Corp, Marubeni Corp and Sumitomo Corp.
Of the 4.232 billion pesos earned, 3.168 billion pesos came from the second payment tranche for the sale of Fort Bonifacio to a consortium led by Metro-Pacific Corp.
The Philippines collected 44 billion pesos from its privatisation programme in 1995, raising privatisation proceeds to 172.2 billion pesos since the programme was launched in 1986.
